title: Intra-Host Diversity and Phylogenetics Reveal the Ecology of Herpesvirus Infections in Wild Bat Communities
author: Haris Malik
license_note: figshare article detail endpoint license.name: CC BY 4.0

steps.instruction: This repository contains the data, phylogenetic trees, BEAST XML files and R scripts used to analyse herpesvirus diversity, host associations, cross-species transmission and inter-roost spread in Neotropical bat communities from Amazonas, Peru. The study was based on 156 bat samples collected from 14 roosts, with mitochondrial cytochrome b sequencing confirming species identities for 139 individuals representing 22 bat species across four families: Phyllostomidae, Molossidae, Emballonuridae and Vespertilionidae. Herpesvirus screening used a pan-herpesvirus DNA polymerase (DPOL) PCR assay combined with Oxford Nanopore amplicon sequencing to detect Alpha-, Beta- and Gammaherpesviruses and to recover within-host viral diversity. The repository includes the sample-level metadata used in the analyses, maximum-likelihood phylogenetic trees for each herpesvirus subfamily, broader mammalian-context trees for Beta- and Gammaherpesviruses, BEAST XML files for discrete-trait GLM analyses, and R scripts for read assignment, phylogenetic visualisation, strain clustering, Bayesian phylogenetic mixed models, and BEAST transition analyses. Together, these files support the analyses reported in the manuscript, including estimates of herpesvirus prevalence, subfamily-specific host associations, intra-host strain diversity, cross-species transmission and inter-roost viral spread. File descriptions Metadata DrBHV_SpecComp_Data.csv Sample-level dataset used for the infection models and downstream analyses. This file includes bat host metadata, sampling site information, herpesvirus detection results, viral subfamily classifications, coinfection/multi-strain infection variables and host/ecological covariates used in the Bayesian phylogenetic GLMMs. Maximum-likelihood tree files SC_AHV_Seqs_aligned_trimmed.fasta.treefile Maximum-likelihood tree for Alphaherpesvirus DPOL sequences generated from the trimmed alignment. This tree was used to place the detected bat Alphaherpesvirus sequences in broader phylogenetic context. SC_BHV_aligned.fasta.treefile Maximum-likelihood tree for bat Betaherpesvirus DPOL sequences. This tree was used for bat-only Betaherpesvirus phylogenetic visualisation and strain clustering. SC_GHV_aligned.fasta.treefile Maximum-likelihood tree for bat Gammaherpesvirus DPOL sequences. This tree was used for bat-only Gammaherpesvirus phylogenetic visualisation and strain clustering. SC_OtherSpp_BHV_aligned_trimmed_cleaned.fasta.treefile Maximum-likelihood tree containing bat Betaherpesvirus sequences together with homologous Betaherpesvirus sequences from other mammalian hosts. This tree was used to assess broader mammalian phylogenetic relationships and the placement of bat-associated Betaherpesviruses relative to non-bat lineages. SC_OtherSpp_GHV_aligned_trimmed_cleaned.fasta.treefile Maximum-likelihood tree containing bat Gammaherpesvirus sequences together with homologous Gammaherpesvirus sequences from other mammalian hosts. This tree was used to assess broader mammalian phylogenetic relationships and the placement of bat-associated Gammaherpesviruses relative to non-bat lineages. BEAST XML files GHVRoost_SampleSizeThesisCorrected_100mil_internal_external.xml BEAST XML file for the Gammaherpesvirus roost discrete-trait GLM analysis. This model was used to evaluate predictors of inter-roost Gammaherpesvirus spread, including internal and external branch components. SC_AO_GHV_alignedSC_GHV_StrictConstant_TPM2FIG4_HostGLM_SampleSizeThesisCorrected_100mil_internal_external.xml BEAST XML file for the Gammaherpesvirus host-species discrete-trait GLM analysis. This model was used to assess predictors of Gammaherpesvirus cross-species transmission among bat host species, including internal and external branch components. SC_BHV_StrictConstant_TVMFIG4_HostGLMM_SampleSizeThesisCorrected_100mil_internal_external_v2.xml BEAST XML file for the Betaherpesvirus host-species discrete-trait GLM analysis. This model was used to assess predictors of Betaherpesvirus cross-species transmission among bat host species, including host phylogenetic distance, ecological overlap and sampling-related predictors. SC_BHV_StrictConstant_TVMFIG4_RoostGLMM_SampleSizeThesisCorrected_100mil_internal_external.xml BEAST XML file for the Betaherpesvirus roost discrete-trait GLM analysis. This model was used to evaluate predictors of inter-roost Betaherpesvirus spread, including geographic distance, least-cost distance, species composition similarity and sampling-related predictors. R scripts SC_HVSubfamily_ReadAssignment.R Assigns BLAST-matched reads to herpesvirus family or subfamily using NCBI taxonomy information associated with the top BLAST hit TaxID. Reads assigned to Alphaherpesvirinae, Betaherpesvirinae or Gammaherpesvirinae were used in downstream subfamily-specific analyses. SC_ML_trees.R Generates and visualises the maximum-likelihood herpesvirus phylogenies used in the manuscript. This includes bat-only trees and broader mammalian-context trees for assessing host-associated structure and broader phylogenetic relationships. SC_StrainClusteringAnalysis.R Performs affinity-propagation clustering on bat-only Betaherpesvirus and Gammaherpesvirus phylogenetic distance matrices. These clusters were used as operational viral strains for analyses of intra-host strain diversity and multi-strain infections. SC_pGLMMs.R Fits Bayesian phylogenetic generalised linear mixed models for herpesvirus infection outcomes using brms . Models include fixed effects for host traits and random effects for site, species and host phylogeny. SC_BHV_BEAST_Analyses.R Processes Betaherpesvirus BEAST output files to calculate Bayes factors for supported host-species and roost transitions, summarise GLM predictor effects, and generate network/map visualisations of cross-species and inter-roost transmission. SC_GHV_BEAST_Analyses.R Processes Gammaherpesvirus BEAST output files to calculate Bayes factors for supported host-species and roost transitions, summarise GLM predictor effects, and generate network/map visualisations of cross-species and inter-roost transmission. Sequences Sequences are available on GenBank ( Accession: PZ532834 - PZ533048 ). Software requirements Analyses were performed using R and BEAST. The main software requirements are: R, with packages including ape , phytools , rotl , brms , posterior , loo , dplyr , tidyr , readr , purrr , tibble , ggplot2 , patchwork , taxize , seqinr , apcluster , ggtree , treeio , RColorBrewer , data.table , stringr , ggraph , igraph , ggtext , ggfx , sf , terra , elevatr , ggspatial , ggrepel and cowplot . BEAST v1.10.4 for discrete-trait phylogenetic analyses. Tracer v1.7.2 for MCMC diagnostic assessment. TreeAnnotator v1.10.4 for generation of maximum clade credibility trees. IQ-TREE2 for maximum-likelihood phylogenetic inference. MAFFT for sequence alignment. Some scripts require internet access to query external resources, including NCBI taxonomy via taxize and host phylogeny retrieval from the Open Tree of Life via rotl .
